A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–D support reliable comparison despite substantial layout changes.

before.justification: V2 reports original MNIST and CIFAR-10 experiments, including SGLD/ULA results, architecture and loss comparisons, and SGD evaluations in Section 5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and adds multiclass MNIST results, SVHN evaluations, and a calibration study across ten random seeds.

M1.justification: The Gibbs/LMC procedures, temperature-integral bound computation, and random-label calibration remain unchanged. The added task applications and calibration analysis do not specify a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: V3 retains binary MNIST/CIFAR-10 evaluation and adds full MNIST ten-class classification plus SVHN experiments. These additions materially broaden task requirements and represented image domains beyond v2's coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 1 compares against four Pérez-Ortiz et al. methods: f_quad, f_lamda, f_classic, and f_bbb, for FCN and CNN architectures. Their results are explicitly taken from the published table. V2 cited this work but did not report this comparison; its SGD comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: V3 introduces a full-dataset MNIST comparison using stated matching FCN/CNN architectures and data-independent priors, alongside 8,000-example SVHN settings. The reported step sizes, minibatches, priors, and stopping rules for the retained binary experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix D.2.9 tests whether calibration depends on random initialization by repeating the Figure 4 SGLD experiments across ten seeds. The existing architecture, loss-function, single-draw, and SGD analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V2 provides no empirical seed-count or uncertainty summaries. V3 reports ten seeds and calibration factors of 0.75 ± 0.02 for MNIST and 0.84 ± 0.02 for CIFAR-10. It does not specify whether the ± quantities represent standard deviations, standard errors, or another measure.

E6.justification: New Table 1 reports FCN test error/bound of 0.0338/0.2470 and CNN values of 0.0182/0.2025 on multiclass MNIST, alongside baseline results. V3 also adds SVHN curves and calibration seed summaries. V2 Tables 1–2 match v3 Tables 2–3; the additions do not establish same-setting improvements over v2.

T1.justification: The principal bounds and proofs are retained. V3 adds positive-density assumptions in Section 4.1, weakens Lemma 3.1's strict monotonicity statement to non-increase, and adds Appendix C.7's Gaussian-linear/ULA calibration argument. The detailed derivation and proposed extensions are deferred.

C1.justification: V3 broadens the stated empirical applicability to SVHN and multiclass classification and claims tighter certificates than the newly compared methods without specialized training. The central generalization and stability claims remain; the newly highlighted Markov-trajectory contribution was already present in v2 Section 4.1.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly describes calibration as lacking rigorous justification. V3 supplies a low-temperature Gaussian-linear rationale and conditional GLM/NTK extensions, while retaining the conclusion's need for further theory. It also interprets the seed study as calibration stability and explicitly calls for further validation of possible transfer to SGD.

D1.justification: Appendix D.1 replaces the anonymous code-access link with a named GitHub repository. V3 documents the SVHN networks as a three-hidden-layer network with 1,000 units per layer and VGG-16. Existing implementation and hyperparameter disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds discussion or citations concerning Clerico, Arora, Syed, and Wibisono. It also acknowledges that Ujváry et al. (2023) used parts of Lemma 3.1 for a similar idea, qualifying the novelty positioning. Most existing related-work discussion remains.

P1.justification: V3 makes wording and terminology edits, revises the contribution list and Section 4 title, and adds appendix subsections, an impact statement, and acknowledgments. The overall section sequence and most existing exposition remain recognizable.

P2.justification: V3 converts the main text from a single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout, substantially resizing and relocating figures and tables. It adds the discretization illustration in Figure 5, the baseline comparison table, and two SVHN figures, and adds explicit random/true-label panel headings.

improvement.justification: The multiclass and SVHN evaluations, competing-certificate comparison, and ten-seed calibration study make the empirical support more informative and address calibration repeatability. The gain remains limited: Appendix C.7 provides only a sketch, general neural-network calibration remains heuristic, and the tighter reported certificates therefore do not resolve the central rigor limitation.
